30.0.s.en: (1) The call to Judah and the tribes to keep the Passover

30.0.0.en: King Hezekiah's fatherhood appears in his care for all the people of God, whether in his own kingdom, which is the southern kingdom of Judah, or in the northern kingdom, most of whose people had been taken captive by Assyria. So he sent letters calling everyone to come to Jerusalem to keep the Passover, as the Law prescribes. He did not send to Judah only, but to Manasseh and Ephraim, because Ephraim represents a large tribe, and so signifies the whole northern kingdom of Israel.

30.1.0.en: King Hezekiah wanted to restore the celebration of the feast of the Passover, but he was not able to keep it at its appointed time in the first month, because he was occupied with cleansing the temple and sanctifying the altar, and because not all the Levites and priests had sanctified themselves. So Hezekiah gathered his counselors to decide when to keep the Passover, and they had three choices before them:

30.1.1.en: 1- To keep the Passover at its appointed time, which is the fourteenth day of the first month, but the priests and Levites who had come to Jerusalem and were prepared for the Passover were few in number, in addition to the difficulty of gathering all the people to Jerusalem at that time.

30.1.2.en: 2- To postpone the celebration of the feast of the Passover to the coming year, but the postponement would be long, and the people might lose their spiritual zeal.

30.1.3.en: 3- The Law provides that whoever is unclean, or on a long journey, at the time of the feast of the Passover in the first month, may keep the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month (Num 9:10, 11). Hezekiah and his counselors settled on the third choice, since they had about a month before them, during which Hezekiah sent messengers to all the priests and Levites to sanctify themselves, and to gather the people in the kingdom of Judah and the rest of the tribes.

30.2.0.en: Beersheba: A city lying in the far south of the kingdom of Judah.

30.2.1.en: Dan: A tribe that dwelt in a region in the far north toward the Sea of Galilee.

30.2.2.en: Hezekiah sent messengers from himself to all the land where the children of Israel dwelt, from the far south, where the city of Beersheba is, to the far north, where the tribe of Dan dwells, to call all the people to come to Jerusalem to keep the Passover, as it is written in the Law of Moses (Ex 12:1-14), especially since the people of God had neglected the celebration of the feast of the Passover for a long time, from the days of Solomon, for it is not mentioned in the Holy Bible that such a Passover was kept since the days of Solomon (v. 26).

30.3.0.en: The couriers who had in their hands letters from King Hezekiah and his princes who assisted him went out and ran to all the cities of Judah and Israel, calling them in the name of the Lord God of their fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Israel, that is, Jacob, to return to Him and worship Him faithfully and keep the feast of the Passover, because God had delivered them from the hand of Assyria and they had remained in their cities, while their brethren had been taken captive by Assyria to scattered lands in the Assyrian kingdom; for the Assyrian captivity took place in stages at the hands of more than one king, so he says, "out of the hand of the kings of Assyria."

30.3.1.en: Here spiritual matters appear, which are:

30.3.2.en: 1- Hezekiah's care for all the people of Israel and not only those in the kingdom of Judah, as we mentioned.

30.3.3.en: 2- He calls his people to return to God to keep the feast of the Passover, that is, to return to their faith and their worship of God, and so obtain His blessing and care.

30.3.4.en: 3- He reminds them of God's grace toward them, that He delivered them, without their brethren, from the Assyrian captivity, so they must thank Him and worship Him faithfully.

30.4.0.en: Astonishment: People came to be astonished and to marvel when they passed through the land of Israel, which Assyria had destroyed, taking many of its people captive.

30.4.1.en: Be ye not stiffnecked: The stubborn animal stiffens its neck, that is, it refuses to submit to its owner and to do the works required of it.

30.4.2.en: The king added these matters in his letters:

30.4.3.en: 1- A call to the people to repent and remember the sins of their fathers, which led to this captivity.

30.4.4.en: 2- A warning against continuing to refuse the worship of God, that is, being unfaithful to Him and occupied with the worship of idols and the lusts of the world, lest they be exposed to destruction a second time, as Assyria did to them.

30.4.5.en: 3- Putting an end to their rebellion against God and their refusal of His worship, since for a long time they had not kept the feast of the Passover.

30.4.6.en: 4- Calling them to come to Jerusalem, to enter the temple of God and worship Him and celebrate the Passover.

30.4.7.en: 5- He gives them the good news that their return to God and His worship removes God's wrath from them and they will be freed from the Assyrian captivity.

30.4.8.en: 6- He warns them that their return to God and their worship of Him brings a blessing to their captive brethren, who had begun to repent and long to return to the temple of God and could not; and when God sees their return, He has compassion on their brethren and brings them back from captivity. For among the clear attributes of God is His great compassion toward the repentant, as He softens the hearts of those who held them captive, so they bring them back to their land, and this is what happened by the hand of Cyrus the Persian king.

30.4.9.en: Repentance is the way of deliverance, which rescues you from all your sins and the troubles that result from them, so hasten to it and do not be lax. On the other hand, do not despair, however grave your sins, because God loves you and waits for you.

30.5.0.en: The couriers set out to all the land of Israel, which is expressed here by Manasseh and Ephraim, but they reached the land possessed by the tribe of Zebulun and did not continue their way northward to Dan and Naphtali. Perhaps this was because of the large presence of the people of God in the region as far as Zebulun, or some obstacles that prevented the couriers from reaching the far north.

30.5.1.en: Strangely, the children of Israel strongly rejected the king's letters, and even laughed to scorn and mocked his messengers, that is, the couriers, because their hearts were attached to the pagan gods and their places of worship, and they forgot their true God, whom their fathers had worshipped.

30.5.2.en: But a small number of them were moved by the king's letters and promised to come to Jerusalem to keep the Passover, for they felt their sins in forsaking the worship of God, and humbled themselves before Him and wanted to return to His worship.

30.5.3.en: Although the Jews in the northern kingdom refused to respond to the king's letters, a small number of them responded, humbled themselves and wanted to return to God. Therefore, servant of God, let there be hope in you that your service is accepted by God and that a small number may respond to it, despite the refusal of the majority. So offer your love and your service and do not be hindered because people reject your words, for God in the end will bring those who are ready, and they are the ones He has chosen.

30.6.0.en: In the kingdom of Judah the people responded to the king's letters and had one heart in returning to God and worshipping Him, so they traveled to Jerusalem. A great multitude gathered and the city was filled with lovers of God and His worship, to keep the feast of the Passover and the feast of Unleavened Bread which follows it, in the second month. Thus the work of God appears, who moved the hearts in the kingdom of Judah to encourage Hezekiah and gladden his heart.

30.7.0.en: The first thing done by the multitude of God's people gathered in Jerusalem was that they removed the pagan altars which the former wicked kings had set up in Jerusalem. For there must be repentance and purity before enjoying the worship of God and fellowship with Him. And they cast the remains of these altars, on which they had offered sacrifices and incense to the idols, into the brook Kidron, which lies east and south of Jerusalem.

30.8.0.en: They stood in their place: The priests and Levites performed their service, each one in his own service. When the priests and Levites saw the zeal and fervor of the people in removing the worship of idols, they were ashamed of their laziness, because they ought to have been leading the people in getting rid of the remains of pagan worship. And the priests and Levites sanctified themselves and began to kill the sacrifices and sprinkle their blood in the temple, as the Levites brought the blood of the sacrifices to the priests, and they sprinkled it on the bronze altar.

30.8.1.en: Thus the priests and Levites returned to performing their service, as prescribed by the Law of Moses, with all care and commitment, and they completed the feast of the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month.

30.9.0.en: A small number of the people of Israel, coming from the tribes outside the kingdom of Judah, responded and came to Jerusalem to keep the Passover, but they had not sanctified themselves according to the Law. So the Levites offered their sacrifices for them, and King Hezekiah prayed to God for them, that He would accept their return to Him despite their weakness in not being sanctified; for when they ate the Passover, God struck them with diseases because of their laxity, but through Hezekiah's prayer God healed them and forgave them for two reasons:

30.9.1.en: 1- Their repentance and return to God and their abandoning the worship of idols, so they prepared their hearts for the worship of God.

30.9.2.en: 2- The intercession and prayer of Hezekiah for them.

30.10.0.en: Those who were prudent: Those who understood God's Law.

30.10.1.en: After the priests and Levites and the people had killed the Passover and kept the feast of the Passover, they began, according to the Law, to keep the feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days, eating unleavened bread and not leavened bread, because leaven signifies evil and unleavened bread signifies purity of heart. And the number seven signifies perfection of purity.

30.10.2.en: During the seven days the Levite singers praised God in His holy temple in great joy. For whoever lives in purity, that is, eats the unleavened bread, can launch out into the praise of God.

30.10.3.en: And King Hezekiah came forward to encourage the priests and Levites, who understood God's Law and who had grieved greatly in the days of the former wicked kings because of the neglect of the worship of God; and through Hezekiah's words they regained their confidence and their faith and were encouraged and rejoiced greatly at the return of the celebration of God's feasts. Perhaps the Levites also rejoiced at the return of a number of their brethren from the tribes to the worship of God in Jerusalem.

30.11.0.en: Because of the great joy of God's people at returning to Him and holding the celebration of the feasts of the Passover and Unleavened Bread, the congregation took counsel and agreed to extend the celebration another week, in addition to what the Law prescribes, especially since the king gave the people a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep. And the princes also gave a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep, so it was a very great religious celebration, and a large number of priests were sanctified, so they were able to offer many sacrifices to God.

30.11.1.en: Although the middle of the second month is the time of harvest, the people's occupation and joy in the worship of God made them extend the celebration another week, that is, they cared for their spiritual life before their material life. And we see the abundance of the gifts of the king and the princes; although the kingdom was poor, they all gave generously and out of their need, and therefore God must have blessed them because of their great love.

30.12.0.en: The strangers: The Gentiles who dwelt with the tribes of Israel and became Jews.

30.12.1.en: The people of God rejoiced, whether those dwelling in the kingdom of Judah, or those coming from the tribes of Israel, and also the stranger proselytes who dwelt among them, because they kept the great feast of the Passover and the feast of Unleavened Bread, especially since no celebration of these feasts with such magnificence had been held since the days of King Solomon, for they kept the feast two weeks, like the days of the dedication of the temple in the time of Solomon, and offered sacrifices in abundance.

30.12.2.en: And the prayers of the people went up, led by the Levites, before the temple of God, so God rejoiced in them, and the priests the Levites blessed the people on behalf of God, and joy and gladness filled the hearts of all.

30.12.3.en: Joy is your natural state as a child of God. If you are occupied with the love of God and His worship, then you can cast all your cares upon Him and feel His hand supporting you and bringing you through the afflictions while you keep your peace and your joy.

30.12.4.en: The people's offerings and their distribution

31.0.s.en: (2) The offering of the tithes and their gathering

31.0.0.en: The gates of the tents of the Lord: The gates of the temple.

31.0.1.en: Hezekiah took care to organize the service in the temple according to what David and Solomon had arranged, and distributed the responsibilities among the priests and Levites, whether in offering the sacrifices, or in the praise, or in any other service.

31.1.0.en: Since worship in the temple had been neglected, the temple was empty of gifts, whether sacrifices or offerings; therefore Hezekiah gave from his own money to complete the worship, which was the morning and evening burnt offerings, and also those offered on the sabbaths and at the new moons and the appointed feasts. And by this he became an example to his people in giving gifts to the house of the Lord.

31.1.1.en: By this Hezekiah's goodness appears, for he was not content with cleansing the temple, nor with beginning the worship in it and sanctifying the altar, but held the feasts of the Passover and Unleavened Bread and encouraged the people to worship God, and also took care for the continuation of the daily worship of God in the temple and the provision of its material needs.

31.2.0.en: Hezekiah's second concern for providing gifts for the house of the Lord appeared in his asking the people dwelling in Jerusalem to give the tithes to God, to provide for the needs of the priests and Levites, that they might be free for the service of God and hold fast to God's Law, which prescribes being devoted to His service; for in the period of neglect of the worship of God in the days of the wicked kings, the priests and Levites were occupied with the works of the world to provide for their necessary needs.

31.3.1.en: Heaps: Piles. The command of King Hezekiah reached not only the regions of the kingdom of Judah, but also the tribes, so the children of Israel, dwelling outside the kingdom of Judah and inside it, took care to give the tithes of wheat, wine, oil, honey and all the produce of the field, and also of the animals, such as oxen and sheep; and because of the abundance of the gifts, they gathered them in heaps.

31.3.2.en: We notice the abundance of the gifts, and this is a proof of two things:

31.3.3.en: 1- The people's care and religious zeal, so they carried out the commandment and gave the tithes and more than that.

31.3.4.en: 2- When God saw the love of His people, He blessed their harvests, their crops and their cattle, so they became abundant.

31.4.0.en: The priests and Levites began to arrange the heaps of gifts, putting each kind of gift by itself, and the gifts continued to increase from the third month, when the wheat is harvested, to the seventh month, in which they gathered the fruits of the various trees. Then King Hezekiah himself came, with the princes of his kingdom, and they saw the abundance of the heaps, so they rejoiced greatly and thanked God, and blessed the people and thanked them for their love and care in carrying out God's commandment.

31.5.0.en: The priests came before Hezekiah, with their chief Azariah, who was of the descendants of Zadok the priest, who lived in the days of David, and Azariah told him of the abundance of the gifts and that the priests and Levites had eaten and been satisfied from them and that this abundance, arranged in heaps, overflowed, and that this was due to God's blessing upon the people and their love and obedience to His commandment.

31.5.1.en: The blessing of the Lord is great for everyone who loves Him, so that he has need of nothing; therefore be careful to give the tithes and the firstfruits, that you may rejoice in God's care and blessings, and above all that your heart may be filled with His love and you may live in fellowship with God that cannot be expressed.

31.6.s.en: (3) The storehouses and the portions of the priests and Levites

31.6.1.en: Hezekiah commanded that chambers be prepared inside the house of the Lord, to be storehouses in which the tithes and all the offerings that the people had given would be put. And he appointed two of the Levites, Cononiah and Shimei his brother, to organize the storehouses, and Hezekiah, with the help of the high priest, also appointed ten Levites to help them in this work.

31.6.2.en: We notice that the gathering of the gifts and their storing was done faithfully by all those in charge, and this of course gladdens the heart of God, so He blesses them, and at the head of all these was the good King Hezekiah.

31.7.0.en: The most holy things: The part of the offerings and sacrifices which is given to the priests and which they eat in the temple (Lev 2:3, 10, 7:6). Likewise Hezekiah and Azariah the high priest appointed a chief over the porters, Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, and set him over the east gate, which is the main gate leading to the temple. His responsibility was to distribute the portions of the priests in the temple and Jerusalem from the offerings and sacrifices, which they must eat in the holy place, that is, beside the temple.

31.7.1.en: Hezekiah also appointed six Levites to help Kore, to distribute portions to the priests and Levites who dwelt in the cities of the kingdom of Judah; for the priests were divided into twenty-four courses, each of which performed the service of the temple for two weeks each year, and the rest of the year they dwelt in their cities, far from Jerusalem. So care began for the needs of the priests and Levites, that they might remain free for the service of God and not need to do the works of the world for their food. And they distributed the portions to all, great and small, that is, the distribution was done faithfully and with care for every individual.

31.8.0.en: Those whom King Hezekiah appointed took care to distribute the portions to the priests and Levites, to all the priests and Levites who were recorded in their genealogies, and also their children and their wives, and they cared for the great and the small to satisfy all, whether those who serve in Jerusalem or those who dwell in the cities of the priests and Levites, whom the lot had not appointed to the service of the house of the Lord.

31.8.1.en: Thus we see that, because of the faithfulness of the priests and Levites, who sanctified themselves and cared for the service of the house of the Lord, God blessed them and gave them all their needs, by putting this care in the heart of the good King Hezekiah.

31.9.0.en: From all that has gone before, the goodness of King Hezekiah appears in the following:

31.9.1.en: 1- His care for the service in the house of the Lord.

31.9.2.en: 2- His holding fast to the commandments and the Law.

31.9.3.en: 3- His faithfulness and exactness in carrying out God's commands.

31.9.4.en: Your goodness and God's acceptance of you are based on the extent of your obedience to His commandments and your faithfulness in carrying them out, so do not be troubled by your weaknesses as long as you try and strive and press on in God's way, for He knows your heart and blesses you in all your steps.

31.9.5.en: The crushing of the Assyrians and the healing of Hezekiah
